# sdrangel

**SDR transceiver and analyser that does several things at once**

- **Version recorded:** 7.27.1
- **Categories:** `listening`, `rf-security`, `sdr`
- **Upstream:** <https://www.sdrangel.org/>

## What it does

A full SDR application built around independent channel plugins: one device's captured bandwidth can feed several demodulators and analysers simultaneously -- AM, FM, SSB, DSD-based digital voice, APT and satellite decoders, ADS-B, packet, a spectrum analyser and a scope -- each in its own panel. It transmits as well as receives on hardware that can, and it drives almost every SDR in common use.

## Why you would want it

It is the most feature-dense SDR application in open source, and the reason to reach for it over gqrx or SDR++ is when you want to do several things to one capture at the same time. Watching a band while decoding two signals in it, or running an analyser alongside a demodulator, is a single window here and three programs fighting over a dongle anywhere else.

## Before it will work

An SDR and its driver library. A capable machine: SDRangel is computationally heavy and benefits from a GPU for its display. On the four targets that do not package it, nothing here installs -- see the note above.

## How it installs

- apt: `sdrangel`
  - **Only Kali carries this.** Measured across all six targets on 2026-08-28: Kali 7.27.1+dfsg-2, and no candidate on Debian 13, Ubuntu 26.04, Parrot or Linux Mint 22.3. `docs/reference/install-verification.md` recorded the same absence from Debian 13 in its Tier 1 probe. It is the last of DragonOS Tier 1's eight new ADD units, and on every target but Kali this manifest will report an apt gap rather than install -- which is the honest answer, not a defect. Upstream publishes .deb artefacts and an AppImage; reaching those needs the binary backend, which M3 has not written yet.

## Known problems

The interface is dense enough to be genuinely hard to start with; the plugin model means almost nothing is where a gqrx user expects it. Its transmit capability is real RF on hardware that can radiate, which is why this entry is categorised rf-security as well as sdr and reaches an operator through a profile requiring explicit opt-in. Debian's build is `+dfsg`, so components that could not be distributed have been removed and a feature present upstream may be absent here.
